subject: Defining crypto custody and operator access for VPC/on-prem private deployment
messages:
From: Anya Patel <anya@medicore.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <t.nguyen@medicore.com>
Date: 2026-07-10T14:02:00Z
Subject: Questions on key custody and operator access for private deployment

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Medicore is actively evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) for clinical data processing, and legal/security have a few non-negotiable asks we need clarified before we proceed:

- Can Redwood ever decrypt customer data under a Private VPC or on‑prem configuration? Who holds the KMS keys?
- If customer-controlled keys are used, do you offer an escrow/emergency recovery option? What are the exact controls for using escrow?
- What operator-level access does Redwood staff retain (support, upgrades, incident response)? Are there documented access boundaries and approval flows?
- Where do audit logs live? Do they contain plaintext identifiers or only hashed/metadata?
- Please provide the current list of subprocessors (particularly any managed services vendors you rely on for deployments) and their geographic locations for data transfers.

I've attached Medicore's initial DPA redlines and a short summary from our legal team. Would appreciate a short written response we can hand to our security/compliance folks; a follow-up call next week would also help.

Best,
Anya
Anya Patel
Head of Legal, Medicore Health
Attachments: Medicore_DPA_redlines_v1.pdf
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>
To: Anya Patel <anya@medicore.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Questions on key custody and operator access for private deployment

Anya — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary up front, then proposed next steps.

Summary answers (short):
- Decrypting customer data: Redwood does not have automatic ability to decrypt customer model inputs/outputs in a VPC or on‑prem private deployment when customer keys are used. We support customer-controlled KMS (customer-managed keys) where key material remains in customer KMS/HSM.
- Escrow/emergency recovery: We can offer a sealed-escrow option as an addendum for disaster scenarios. Escrow unlock requires a documented three-party approval (customer security lead + two named Redwood executives) and is audited in an immutable log.
- Operator access: Standard operator access is limited to orchestration and host-level metrics; we do not expose model plaintext. Access scopes and justifications are captured in an access matrix we can attach.
- Audit logs: Logs are configurable; by default they include operational metadata (timestamps, request IDs, token counts). We can provide a privacy-preserving schema that excludes raw content and stores only hashed identifiers.
- Subprocessors: We rely on a small set of deployment partners for certain on‑prem components (infrastructure integrators) — full list attached and mapped by country.

Proposed next steps:
1) I attached a short Redwood summary document (RW-priv-deploy-key-model-summary.docx) that maps out three custody flavors: customer KMS (preferred), customer KMS + sealed escrow, and customer-provided HSM with attestation.
2) Can we set a 30-min call next week with your security and legal to walk the escrow controls and log schema?
3) Rishi (cc'd) will follow with the technical runbook and a brief on how KV cache and model artifacts are encrypted in the private runtime.

I realize Medicore is sensitive about any path that could leave you without control over keys — we are prepared to make the contractual commitments needed (DPA language + operational runbook) to satisfy that.

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Director, Security & Privacy Ops
Redwood Inference
Attachments: RW-priv-deploy-key-model-summary.docx
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com>
To: Anya Patel <anya@medicore.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.example.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2026-07-14T11:07:00Z
Subject: Re: Questions on key custody and operator access for private deployment

Anya / team — following Laura's overview, a slightly deeper technical picture of the three deployment options and the safeguards we implement: 

1) Customer-managed KMS (recommended)
- Keys never leave customer KMS/HSM. Redwood services use KMIP/Cloud KMS APIs to request crypto operations (sign/decrypt) where supported; plaintext is not returned to Redwood.
- Tokenization / KV cache: caches are encrypted with a per-node ephemeral key that is encrypted under the customer key; without the customer KMS, the ephemeral keys are unusable.
- Key rotation: supported; we provide a rotation handshake to rewrap ephemeral keys.

2) Customer KMS + Sealed Escrow (for operational continuity)
- Escrow keys are held encrypted in a split-seal (Shamir split) across two HSM partitions and a sealed file stored on customer-controlled S3/Blob.
- Escrow unlock policy: requires written request from the customer security lead + two named Redwood execs; all unlock actions are recorded to a tamper-evident ledger (we can provide attestation).
- We can make this workflow binding in the SOW and DPA annex.

3) Customer-provided HSM / on‑prem HSM with attestation
- We integrate with customer HSM via PKCS#11; Redwood only receives proof-of-decryption success/failure; we never store key material.

Operator access boundaries (practical controls):
- Support access is role-based and time-limited; no role can decrypt model inputs/outputs.
- Emergency support: access elevation requires the escrow unlock workflow above and multi-person approval.
- All maintenance sessions are recorded; logs are stored in customer-account S3 for retention policy control.

Audit logs and schema: we propose a minimal schema that records request-id, timestamp, model-id, latency, and a one-way hash of a customer-provided request fingerprint. We will not log request content or PII fields unless explicitly authorized in writing.

I attached the internal runbook excerpt (runbook-priv-deploy-keyflow.pdf) and an internal runbook id (INTRUNBOOK-4523) for your security team to review. Happy to show the flow in a quick technical session.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: runbook-priv-deploy-keyflow.pdf
From: Tom Nguyen <t.nguyen@medicore.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Anya Patel <anya@medicore.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2026-07-17T10:58:00Z
Subject: Re: Questions on key custody and operator access for private deployment

Laura / Rishi — thanks for the detail. A few follow-ups after an internal review: 

- Escrow: Medicore is extremely cautious about any escrow that could be used to access keys. The split-seal approach is interesting, but we need a written and enforceable guarantee that Redwood will never be able to unilaterally decrypt without explicit customer authorization recorded in the escrow policy (no backdoors). Suggest specific DPA language we can review that enumerates the approval steps and auditability.
- Logs: we need a sample log extract (sanitized) showing the proposed fields and their formats. Also confirmation that logs will reside in our region (US-east) and that retention settings are customer-controlled.
- Subprocessors: please provide the full current list with company names, contact persons, and country of operations. Any vendor with potential access to metadata must be listed.

We have two asks before scheduling a SOC-level technical review: 1) Redwood to provide the escrow policy text and 2) a sanitized sample log extract. After that, we can set a 45-min call with our security and compliance teams.

Can Marcus from CloudBroker (cc'd) help coordinate the logistics for the on‑prem install and provide his vendor details?

Thanks,
Tom Nguyen
CISO, Medicore Health
